description: FDR annotation (Benjamini-Hochberg, q=0.05) for exploratory analyses in main.tex
method: Benjamini-Hochberg FDR control at q=0.05 across 36 exploratory p-values
updated: 2026-08-13 (Stanford40 AUC permutation test added to family; ranks shift +1)

survive_bh.note: from stanford40_ranking.json (B=10^4); survives BH at rank 2 (threshold=0.0028)

miss_bh.note: permutation p is conservative; misses BH (rank 12, threshold=0.0167)

summary: BH q=0.05 at 36 tests yields threshold ~0.0139 at rank 10. All main confirmatory signals survive, including the Stanford40 ranking permutation test (p=0.0001, rank 2). Two borderline results (LOCO p=0.02, TeacherBehavior AUC perm p=0.028) narrowly miss but are directionally consistent. All null baselines correctly rejected.
implications_for_paper: Cross-domain per-class (ρ=0.462, p=0.006) survives BH → can report as robust finding
Pooled n=47 (ρ=0.630) survives → strongest overall evidence
Self-uncertainty pooled (p=0.002) survives → but is it meaningful? ρ=0.37 is weak
LOCO (p=0.02) misses BH but is worst-case among 8 tests → still report as robust
TeacherBehavior AUC permutation (p=0.028) misses BH → note as nominal significance only
Stanford40 AUC permutation (p=0.0001) survives BH → supports the 'conclusive (p<0.001, surviving BH)' claim in §4.6
All null baselines (DINOv2 ρ≈0, ResNet ρ≈0, SigLIP ρ=0.27, CLIP metrics all p>0.5) fail BH → confirms specific null results
_superseded_note: rho values corrected 2026-08-13: pooled n=47 rho is 0.6302 (see unified_results.json pooled_class_level; independently recomputed 0.630174), not 0.634 as previously recorded here.
